94:   -- We know d(Uᵢ, C) ≤ d(Uᵢ, Mᵢ) because Mᵢ ∈ C (from h_rows M hM_mem i)
95:   have dist_le_dist : Δ₀(Uᵢ, C) ≤ Δ₀(Uᵢ, Mᵢ) := by
96:     apply csInf_le' -- Using sInf property
97:     --  ⊢ ↑Δ₀(Uᵢ, Mᵢ) ∈ {d | ∃ v ∈ ↑MC, ↑Δ₀(Uᵢ, v) ≤ d}
98:     simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Nat.cast_le]

112: /-- Extracts the constructed codewords V₀, V₁ and their agreement properties.
113: Hypotheses: 1. more than ε affine combinations Uᵣ are close to C^m (`hR_star_card`),
114: 2. the base code C features proximity gaps for affine lines (`hC_gap`)
115: => This function constructs the corresponding `interleaved codewords` `V₀` and `V₁` in `C^m`
116: that exhibit correlated agreement with `U₀` and `U₁` row-by-row respectively.
117: It returns a tuple containing:
118: - `V₀`, `V₁` : Codewords in `C^m`
119: - `hRowWise_pair_CA`: `Δ₀((u₀ := getRow U₀ rowIdx) ⋈₂ (u₁ := getRow U₁ rowIdx),`
120:                           `(v₀ := getRow V₀ rowIdx) ⋈₂ (v₁ := getRow V₁ rowIdx)) ≤ e`
121: -/
122: def constructInterleavedCodewordsAndRowWiseCA
123:     (U₀ U₁ : InterleavedWord A (Fin m) ι)
124:   (hC_gap : e_ε_correlatedAgreementAffineLinesNat (F := F) (C := C) e ε)
125:   (hR_star_card : (R_star (F := F) (C := C) (m := m) (e := e) U₀ U₁).card > ε) :
126:   Σ' (V₀ V₁ : C ^⋈ (Fin m)), -- Σ' creates a dependent tuple
127:     ∀ rowIdx, pairJointProximity₂ (u₀ := getRow U₀ rowIdx)
128:       (u₁ := getRow U₁ rowIdx)
129:       (v₀ := getRow (show (InterleavedCodeword A (Fin m) ι C) from V₀) rowIdx)
130:       (v₁ := getRow (show (InterleavedCodeword A (Fin m) ι C) from V₁) rowIdx) e := by
131:   let V₀₁ : (rowIdx: Fin m)
132:     → Σ' (v₀ v₁ : C), pairJointProximity₂ (u₀ := getRow U₀ rowIdx)
133:     (u₁ := getRow U₁ rowIdx) (v₀ := v₀) (v₁ := v₁) e := fun rowIdx => by
134:     set u₀ := getRow U₀ rowIdx
135:     set u₁ := getRow U₁ rowIdx
136:     -- Need: Δ₀(u₀ ⋈₂ u₁, v₀ ⋈₂ v₁) ≤ e, this requires { r | (1 - r) • u₀ + r • u₁ ∈ C} > ε,
137:       -- which can be derived from hR_star_card
138:     -- For any row i, R_star_card implies the proximity gap property applies to that row
139:     have h_P_affineCombineRow:
140:       (Pr_{ let r ←$ᵖ F }[ -- Probability notation
141:         (Δ₀(affineLineEvaluation (F := F) u₀ u₁ r, C) ≤ e: Prop)
142:       ] > ((ε: ℝ≥0) / (Fintype.card F : ℝ≥0))) := by
143:       -- Goal: Show probability > ε / q
144:       -- We know: card R* > ε, where R* = {r | Δ₀(Uᵣ, C^m) ≤ e}
145:       -- Let R_line = {r | Δ₀((Uᵣ)ᵢ, C) ≤ e}
146:       -- We proved earlier: R* ⊆ R_line
147:       -- So, card R_line ≥ card R* > ε
148:       let R_star_set := R_star (F := F) (C := C) (m := m) (e := e) U₀ U₁
149:       let R_line_set := Finset.filter (fun r =>
150:           Δ₀(affineLineEvaluation (F := F) u₀ u₁ r, C) ≤ e) Finset.univ
151:       -- Prove R* ⊆ R_line
152:       have R_star_subset : R_star_set ⊆ R_line_set := by
153:         intro r hr_mem
154:         simp only [R_star, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, R_star_set] at hr_mem
155:         simp only [R_line_set, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
156:         -- Use dist_row_le_dist_ToInterleavedCode
157:         let Uᵣ : InterleavedWord A (Fin m) ι := affineLineEvaluation U₀ U₁ r
158:         have h_dist_le := dist_row_le_dist_ToInterleavedCode C Uᵣ rowIdx
159:         have h_row_eq : affineLineEvaluation u₀ u₁ r = getRow Uᵣ rowIdx := by
160:           ext j;
161:           simp only [affineLineEvaluation, Word, Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, getRow,
162:             InterleavedWord.getRowWord, Matrix.transpose_apply, Uᵣ]
163:           have h_u₀_j : u₀ j = U₀ j rowIdx := by rfl
164:           have h_u₁_j : u₁ j = U₁ j rowIdx := by rfl
165:           rw [h_u₀_j, h_u₁_j]
166:         rw [←h_row_eq] at h_dist_le
167:         exact le_trans h_dist_le hr_mem
168:       -- Use cardinality argument
169:       have h_card_line_gt_eps : R_line_set.card > ε :=
170:         lt_of_lt_of_le hR_star_card (Finset.card_le_card R_star_subset)
171:       -- Convert cardinality to probability: `Pr[P r] = card {r | P r} / card F`
172:       simp only [ENNReal.coe_natCast]
173:       rw [prob_uniform_eq_card_filter_div_card]
174:       simp only [ENNReal.coe_natCast]
175:       rw [gt_iff_lt]
176:       apply ENNReal.div_lt_div_right
177:       · simp only [ne_eq, Nat.cast_eq_zero, Fintype.card_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true]
178:       · exact ENNReal.natCast_ne_top (Fintype.card F)
179:       · exact Nat.cast_lt.mpr h_card_line_gt_eps
180:     -- Apply proximity gap of C to get correlated agreement at this row
181:     have h_corr_agree_row: Δ₀(u₀ ⋈₂ u₁, C ^⋈ (Fin 2)) ≤ e := by
182:       exact hC_gap (u₀) (u₁) (h_P_affineCombineRow)
183:     have hne : Nonempty ↑(C ^⋈ (Fin 2)) := instNonemptyInterleavedCode (κ := Fin 2) (C := C)
184:     let V_rowIdx := @Code.pickClosestCodeword_of_Nonempty_Code _ _ _ _ (C ^⋈ (Fin 2)) hne (u₀ ⋈₂ u₁)
185:     let v₀ := getRow (show (InterleavedCodeword A (Fin 2) ι C) from V_rowIdx) 0
186:     let v₁ := getRow (show (InterleavedCodeword A (Fin 2) ι C) from V_rowIdx) 1
187:     use v₀, v₁
188:     have h_dist_min := @Code.distFromPickClosestCodeword_of_Nonempty_Code
189:       _ _ _ _ (C ^⋈ (Fin 2)) hne (u₀ ⋈₂ u₁)
190:     rw [h_dist_min] at h_corr_agree_row
191:     have h_v₀_interleaved_v₁ : (V_rowIdx).val = (v₀.val ⋈₂ v₁.val) := by
192:       -- apply Subtype.ext;
193:       funext colIdx rowIdx₀₁
194:       by_cases h : rowIdx₀₁ = 0
195:       · rw [h]; rfl
196:       · have h' : rowIdx₀₁ = 1 := by omega
197:         rw [h']; rfl
198:     unfold pairJointProximity₂
199:     rw [h_v₀_interleaved_v₁] at h_corr_agree_row; exact_mod_cast h_corr_agree_row
200:   let V₀_wordStack : WordStack A (Fin m) ι := fun rowIdx => (V₀₁ rowIdx).1.val
201:   let V₁_wordStack : WordStack A (Fin m) ι := fun rowIdx => (V₀₁ rowIdx).2.1.val
202:   let V₀ : C ^⋈ (Fin m) := ⟨⋈| V₀_wordStack, by
203:     simp only [Word, interleavedCodeSet,
204:       interleavedCode_eq_interleavedCodeSet, WordStack, InterleavedWord,
205:       interleave_wordStack_eq, Set.mem_setOf_eq,
206:       Matrix.transpose_transpose]
207:     intro rowIdx; exact Subtype.coe_prop (V₀₁ rowIdx).fst
208:   ⟩
209:   let V₁ : C ^⋈ (Fin m) := ⟨⋈| V₁_wordStack, by
210:     simp only [Word, interleavedCodeSet,
211:       interleavedCode_eq_interleavedCodeSet, WordStack, InterleavedWord,
212:       interleave_wordStack_eq, Set.mem_setOf_eq,
213:       Matrix.transpose_transpose]
214:     intro rowIdx; exact Subtype.coe_prop (V₀₁ rowIdx).snd.fst
215:   ⟩
216:   use V₀, V₁
217:   intro rowIdx
218:   exact (V₀₁ rowIdx).2.2 -- definitional equality of V₀ V₁ according to V₀₁
219: 
220: open Classical in
221: omit [NoZeroDivisors F] [DecidableEq F] [Fintype A] [Module.Free F A] in
222: /-- **Lemma 3.2 (DG25): Closeness implies Closeness to Constructed Codeword**
223: Context:
224: - `C` is a linear code in `F^n` with proximity gaps for affine lines (params `e`, `ε`).
225: - `e` is within the unique decoding radius of `C`.
226: - `U₀, U₁` are ColWise-interleaved words.
227: - `R*` is the set of `r` in `F` such that `Uᵣ = (1-r)U₀ + rU₁` is `e`-close to `C^m`.
228: - `V₀, V₁` are specific codewords in `C^m` constructed row-by-row using `C`'s gap property,
229:   assuming `|R*| > ε`.
230: - `Vᵣ = (1-r)V₀ + rV₁`.
231: Statement: For any parameter `r` in `R*`, the matrix `Uᵣ` must be `e`-close to the codeword `Vᵣ`.
232:  Lemma 3.2: Given a linear code `C ⊂ F^n` with proximity gaps for affine lines
233: (parameters `e`, `ε`), its `m`-fold interleaving `C^m`, and two matrices
234: `U_0`, `U_1 ∈ F^{m × n}`, let `U_r = (1-r)U_0 + rU_1` be a point on the affine line between them,
235: and let `R* = { r ∈ F | d^m(U_r, C^m) ≤ e }` be the set of parameters yielding points close
236: to the interleaved code.
237: -/
238: lemma affineWord_close_to_affineInterleavedCodeword
239:     (U₀ U₁ : InterleavedWord A (Fin m) ι)
240:   (he : e ≤ (Code.uniqueDecodingRadius (F := A) (ι := ι) (C := MC)))", "truncated": false}

364:     (f g : α → Prop)

section TupleRight

/-! In the previous section, we have discussed inserting or removing elements on the left of a
tuple. In this section, we do the same on the right. A difference is that `Fin (n+1)` is constructed
inductively from `Fin n` starting from the left, not from the right. This implies that Lean needs
more help to realize that elements belong to the right types, i.e., we need to insert casts at
several places. -/

variable {α : Fin (n + 1) → Sort*} (x : α (last n)) (q : ∀ i, α i)
  (p : ∀ i : Fin n, α i.castSucc) (i : Fin n) (y : α i.castSucc) (z : α (last n))

/-- The beginning of an `n+1` tuple, i.e., its first `n` entries -/
def init (q : ∀ i, α i) (i : Fin n) : α i.castSucc :=
  q i.castSucc

theorem init_def {q : ∀ i, α i} :
    (init fun k : Fin (n + 1) ↦ q k) = fun k : Fin n ↦ q k.castSucc :=
  rfl

/-- Adding an element at the end of an `n`-tuple, to get an `n+1`-tuple. The name `snoc` comes from
`cons` (i.e., adding an element to the left of a tuple) read in reverse order. -/
def snoc (p : ∀ i : Fin n, α i.castSucc) (x : α (last n)) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : α i :=
  if h : i.val < n then _root_.cast (by rw [Fin.castSucc_castLT i h]) (p (castLT i h))
  else _root_.cast (by rw [eq_last_of_not_lt h]) x

@[simp]

lemma comp_contractNth {β : Sort*} (opα : α → α → α) (opβ : β → β → β) {f : α → β}
    (hf : ∀ x y, f (opα x y) = opβ (f x) (f y)) (j : Fin (n + 1)) (g : Fin (n + 1) → α) :

/-- To show two sigma pairs of tuples agree, it to show the second elements are related via
`Fin.cast`. -/
theorem sigma_eq_of_eq_comp_cast {α : Type*} :
    ∀ {a b : Σ ii, Fin ii → α} (h : a.fst = b.fst), a.snd = b.snd ∘ Fin.cast h → a = b
  | ⟨ai, a⟩, ⟨bi, b⟩, hi, h => by
    dsimp only at hi
    subst hi
    simpa using h

/-- `Fin.sigma_eq_of_eq_comp_cast` as an `iff`. -/
theorem sigma_eq_iff_eq_comp_cast {α : Type*} {a b : Σ ii, Fin ii → α} :
    a = b ↔ ∃ h : a.fst = b.fst, a.snd = b.snd ∘ Fin.cast h :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ h ▸ ⟨rfl, funext <| Fin.rec fun _ _ ↦ rfl⟩, fun ⟨_, h'⟩ ↦
    sigma_eq_of_eq_comp_cast _ h'⟩

end Fin

/-- `Π i : Fin 2, α i` is equivalent to `α 0 × α 1`. See also `finTwoArrowEquiv` for a
non-dependent version and `prodEquivPiFinTwo` for a version with inputs `α β : Type u`. -/
@[simps -fullyApplied]
def piFinTwoEquiv (α : Fin 2 → Type u) : (∀ i, α i) ≃ α 0 × α 1 where
  toFun f := (f 0, f 1)
  invFun p := Fin.cons p.1 <| Fin.cons p.2 finZeroElim
  left_inv _ := funext <| Fin.forall_fin_two.2 ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
